'''Bloch's principle''' is a [[philosophy|philosophical]] principle in [[mathematics]]
stated by [[André Bloch (mathematician)|André Bloch]].<ref>{{cite news|first=A.|last=Bloch|
title=La conception actuelle de la theorie de fonctions entieres et meromorphes|journal=Enseignement Mathématique|year=1926| volume=25|pages=83–103}}</ref>

Bloch states the principle in Latin as: ''Nihil est in infinito quod non prius fuerit in finito,'' and explains this as follows:  Every proposition in whose statement the [[actual infinity]] occurs can be always considered a consequence, almost immediate, of a proposition where it does not occur, a proposition in ''finite terms''.

Bloch mainly applied this principle to the theory of [[function (mathematics)|functions]] of a [[complex variable]].  Thus, for example, according to this principle, [[Picard's theorem]] corresponds to [[Schottky's theorem]], and [[Bloch's theorem (complex variables)|Valiron's theorem]] corresponds to [[Bloch's theorem (complex variables)|Bloch's theorem]].

Based on his Principle, Bloch was able to predict or conjecture several
important results such as the [[Ahlfors theory|Ahlfors's Five Islands theorem]],
[[Henri Cartan|Cartan]]'s theorem on holomorphic curves omitting hyperplanes,<ref name=Lang>{{cite book |last=Lang | first=Serge | title=Introduction to Complex Hyperbolic Spaces | publisher=Springer | publication-place=New York | year=2010 | isbn=978-1-4419-3082-8}}</ref> [[Walter Hayman|Hayman]]'s result that an exceptional set of radii is unavoidable in [[Nevanlinna theory]].

In the more recent times several general theorems were proved which can be regarded as rigorous statements in the spirit of the Bloch Principle:

==Zalcman's lemma==

A family <math>\mathcal F</math> of functions [[meromorphic]] on the unit disc <math>\Delta</math> is not [[Normal family|normal]] if and only if there exist:
* a number <math>0 < r < 1</math>
* points <math>z_n,</math> <math>|z_n|<r</math>
* functions <math>f_n \in \mathcal F</math>
* numbers <math>\rho_n \to 0 +</math>
such that <math>f_n(z_n+\rho_n \zeta)\to g(\zeta), </math>
spherically uniformly on compact subsets of <math>C,</math> where <math>g</math> is a nonconstant meromorphic function on <math>C.</math><ref>{{cite journal|first=L.|last=Zalcman|
title=Heuristic principle in complex function theory|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|
volume=82|year=1975|issue=8|pages=813–817|doi=10.1080/00029890.1975.11993942}}</ref>

Zalcman's lemma may be generalized to several complex variables. First, define the following:

A family <math>\mathcal F</math> of holomorphic functions on a domain <math>\Omega\subset C^n</math> is normal in <math>\Omega</math> if every sequence of functions <math>\{f_j\}\subseteq \mathcal F</math> contains either a subsequence which converges to a limit function <math>f \ne \infty</math> uniformly on each compact subset of <math>\Omega,</math> or a subsequence which converges uniformly to <math>\infty</math> on each compact subset.

For every function <math>\varphi</math> of class <math>C^2(\Omega) </math> define at each point <math>z\in \Omega</math> a Hermitian form
<math> L_z(\varphi, v):=\sum_{k,l=1}^n \frac{\partial^2\varphi}{\partial z_k \partial \overline{z}_l}(z) v_k \overline{v}_l \ \ (v\in C^n), </math>
and call it the Levi form of the function <math>\varphi</math> at <math>z.</math>

If function <math>f</math> is holomorphic on <math>\Omega,</math> set
<math> f^\sharp (z):=\sup_{ |v|=1}\sqrt{L_z(\log(1+|f|^2), v)}. </math>
This quantity is well defined since the Levi form <math>L_z(\log(1+|f|^2), v)</math> is nonnegative for all <math>z\in \Omega.</math>
In particular, for <math> n = 1 </math> the above formula takes the form
<math> f^\sharp (z):=\frac{|f'(z)|}{1+|f(z)|^2} </math>
and <math>z^\sharp</math> coincides with the spherical metric on <math>C.</math>

The following characterization of normality can be made based on [[Marty's theorem]], which states that a family is normal if and only if the spherical derivatives are locally bounded:<ref>{{cite journal | last=Dovbush | first=P. V. | title=Zalcman's lemma in C n | journal=Complex Variables and Elliptic Equations | volume=65 | issue=5 | date=2020 | issn=1747-6933 | doi=10.1080/17476933.2019.1627529 | pages=796–800 | doi-access=free }}</ref>

Suppose that the family <math> \mathcal F </math> of functions holomorphic on <math>\Omega\subset C^n</math> is not normal at some point <math>z_0\in \Omega.</math> Then there exist sequences <math> f_j\in \mathcal F,</math> <math>z_j\to z_0,</math> <math>\rho_j=1/f_j^\sharp(z_j)\to 0,</math> such that the sequence <math>g_j(z)=f_j(z_j+\rho_j z) </math> converges locally uniformly in <math>C^n </math> to a non-constant entire function <math>g</math> satisfying <math>g^\sharp(z)\leq g^\sharp(0)=1</math>

==Brody's lemma==

Let ''X'' be a [[compact space|compact]] [[complex analytic manifold]], such that every [[holomorphic map]] from the [[complex plane]]
to ''X'' is constant. Then there exists a [[metric (mathematics)|metric]] on ''X'' such that every holomorphic map from the unit disc with the [[Poincaré metric]] to ''X'' does not increase distances.<ref name=Lang />
